layers.nodata_definition: Pixels without a value in NASA's raster (outside the swath, water mask, decorrelation) come back from the ImageServer as the requested no-data -9999 (NaN and the service fill |v| > 1e30 are treated the same); they are drawn fully transparent (alpha 0). No gap is filled with 0; the built rasters contain no pixel with the exact value 0 (audit 2026-11-14).

scale._doc: Same range as NASA's web map stretch (-40 to 40 cm); low values blue, high values red; values beyond the range are drawn at the end colour.

value_range.note: Values in the file run from -47.56 to 55.45 cm (1st-99th percentile -16.55 to 36.85 cm); 0.59 % of the valid pixels lie outside the colour scale's -40 to +40 cm and are drawn in the end colour, so the colours do not show their full size. The scale is NASA's web-map stretch, not the data range.

geometry.los_look_direction: about 40 degrees off vertical, slightly south of due west
geometry.sign_note: NASA's item says positive is towards the satellite (east and up on ascending tracks, west and up on the descending track). Project check on 2026-11-13 (point values across the coast at 67.0-68.0 W): ascending values rise to about +45 cm just south of the fault and the descending track is negative there, while NASA's Earth Observatory article reports westward motion south of the fault. For a left-looking ascending pass, westward motion is away from the satellite, so the published sign description and the values disagree; the sign is not confirmed. Show values by number, not by direction words, until NASA JPL confirms.
geometry.look_side_basis: NISAR L-SAR looks left; consistent with NASA's stated look directions for these tracks
geometry.sign_missing: Not established from product documentation (read 2026-11-14): (1) the formula and sign NASA JPL used to turn the Urgent Response GUNW unwrapped phase into these '_cm' layers (not published with the item or the ImageServer); (2) the GUNW interferogram phase convention (reference x conj(secondary) or the reverse): the NISAR user guide (nisar-docs.asf.alaska.edu, GUNW and phase pages) does not state it, and the product specification JPL D-102272 Rev E could be downloaded but its text could not be extracted in this environment; (3) the line-of-sight unit vectors and platform heading of these Urgent Response granules (not listed in CMR; the provisional GUNW files need an Earthdata login). Documented: NISAR is left-looking (nisar-docs.asf.alaska.edu/nisar-intro); NASA's item gives the look directions and 'positive = towards the satellite'.

layers.covers_note: The pair spans 2026-06-24 22:04:31.806Z (M7.2) and 22:05:04.053Z (M7.5): the map is the sum of both shocks and of any aftershock and post-seismic motion until 2026-06-25; it cannot separate them.

layers.legend: Line-of-sight displacement, cm (−40 to +40) · NASA JPL NISAR, 13–25 Jun 2026
layers.note: Covers both shocks of 24 June. Preliminary (predicted orbits), not calibrated to the ground. Sign not confirmed; colours stop at ±40 cm, some values are larger. Transparent = no data, not zero motion.

It is not the number of damaged buildings in Venezuela: buildings outside these areas, and parts not analysed, were not graded.

layers.visible: 10 m true colour: shows the coast, the airport, streets, open ground and fresh bare slopes, but not single damaged buildings. Building damage in Caraballeda and Catia La Mar graded by Copernicus EMS from sub-metre images cannot be seen at this resolution; a difference between the two dates is not by itself evidence of damage (light, haze, season, construction, cleanup).
